text:
tammy: Heads up — we've got a spike of 502s to /v1/models/large in eu-west from some customers. Error rate jumped ~4x at 10:03 UTC.
ryan: Seen similar alerts. Any pattern on client IPs? IPv6 vs IPv4?
sai: Initial logs show clients resolving AAAA and connecting over IPv6. But the edge node egress path sometimes ends up via a NAT64 prefix and we see translation in the gateway logs.
maria: Wait, NAT64 in our path? Which datacenter is doing translation — should be local.
sai: Looks like the node in eu-west1 is forwarding to a transit that has NAT64 in us-central for a subset of pods; routing decision seems wrong.
ton: (ops-bot) incident created: INC-2026-0312-17 — triage started :rotating_light:
ryan: Can someone curl the endpoint forcing v6/v4 to reproduce?
oncall-jordan: repro: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:2604:abc::1 https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/models/large` -> TLS handshake fails with SNI mismatch on translated connection.
tammy: Logs: `tls: server name "api.redwood-inference.internal" doesn't match certificate for 10.8.2.5` — that's from the NAT64-adjacent proxy.
sai: So translation is rewriting destination to backend IPv4 addr and the cert presented is from an internal LB that expects SNI for the IPv4 host. When client used IPv6 it expects hostname cert to match; translation path swaps to different LB.
ryan: Could be service discovery returning mixed A/AAAA in different orders. If the client prefers AAAA but DNS split-horizon returns IPv4-first in upstream, our egress chooses a path that breaks TLS.
maria: Also saw weird TTL differences: AAAA had low TTL, A had long TTL. Possibly a DNS layer (external) swapping records to steer traffic.
sai: Quick debug commands I ran: `dig +short AAAA api.eu-west.internal` -> `2604:abc::1\ndig +short A api.eu-west.internal` -> `34.120.11.5`
ryan: Envoy config on the node — what does cluster.connect_timeout and dns_lookup_family look like? If it's set to V4_PREFERRED it might prefer IPv4 even when AAAA exists.
sai: Node config is dns_lookup_family: AUTO. But kube-proxy iptables rules and outbound policy also matter. I found `haproxy` on the egress box with `option ipv6` disabled for the backend pool.
oncall-jordan: Ops-bot ran a quick mitigation: set iptables rule to prefer v6 for that service pool. Pushed at 10:12 UTC.
ton: (infra-bot) config-change: egress/haproxy - enabled backend ipv6 flag (rolled back in 5m if failure)
tammy: After the mitigation error rate dropped back to baseline for most tenants but a few still saw errors.
maria: For the remaining customers, their clients embed IP literals in callbacks (bad), so when NAT64 rewrites it we end up with wrong host header. Need to add guardrails.
sai: Root causes summary so far: 1) split A/AAAA ordering and inconsistent TTLs from DNS steering 2) egress proxy (haproxy/envoy) backend not symmetric for v6/v4 leading to SNI/cert mismatches 3) NAT64 applying in unexpected region due to routing asymmetry.
ryan: Proposed short-term fixes: prefer IPv6 in node resolver for service namespace, force dualstack LB to present same cert on both v4/v6 frontends, and add a translation-safe SNI policy.
maria: Longer-term: ensure our service discovery returns consistent A/AAAA pairs with aligned TTLs, advertise consistent origin across any NAT64 boxes, and add probes exercising both v4 and v6 paths in CI.
tammy: Can someone file two follow-ups: (1) infra task to audit egress proxies for ipv6 parity; (2) dns team to unify TTLs and make dualstack ordering deterministic.
ryan: I'll take the proxy audit. Will check envoy/haproxy templates and any HAProxy ACLs that differ per family.
sai: I'll work with networking to trace BGP exits that routed to the NAT64 transit and why that path was chosen.
oncall-jordan: ops-bot: rollback note: the iptables v6 preference will be reverted after 30m if no thumbs up.
maria: Add test case: `curl -6` vs `curl -4` should hit same backend and return identical cert chain. Add to perf/edge tests.
tammy: Also add alert: spike in TLS verification failures with reason contains "doesn't match certificate" -> auto-pager.
ryan: FYI config snippet I found in haproxy that was problematic: ```backend model-backends
  mode tcp
  balance leastconn
  server s1 34.120.11.5:443 check
  # missing ipv6 server entry
```
sai: Suggested runtime flag for kube-proxy: `--dual-stack-prefer-ipv6` (pseudo) — we should document and possibly enable for eu-west where IPv6 demand is higher.
maria: Any cost implications? If we start preferring IPv6 we may avoid extra NAT64 egress charges and cross-region hops; win on latency and cost.
tammy: Good point. Add cost estimate to the infra ticket.
ryan: I'll drop a short postmortem once we close tasks. Thanks everyone. :heart:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0312-17 marked resolved at 10:33 UTC (error rate back to baseline).
